---
title: "Implementing RRP: A Simulated Hospital Walkthrough"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(readmit)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
```

# A hospital's changing question

Harbor General wants to see how remaining readmission risk changes after a
patient leaves the hospital. A single discharge prediction cannot describe what
was knowable several days later. Readmission Risk Pool (RRP) repeats an assessment
at chosen times, retains each result, and derives views of current risk and
recorded trajectories. The `readmit` package supplies that structure; the
hospital supplies its source mapping and risk model.

For an eligible discharge episode, the target is the probability of a **first
readmission strictly after the assessment time and through 30 elapsed days after
the original discharge**. Each assessment has less follow-up remaining. A known
readmission or death makes an episode ineligible. An event's occurrence time
may differ from the time its record became available. The example below uses
both times so earlier assessments do not acquire later knowledge.

Everything here is simulated for teaching. The model is neither clinically
validated nor evidence that acting on its estimates improves outcomes. Run the
article with `readmit`, `dplyr`, and `tidyr` installed; its website build also
uses `rmarkdown` and `pkgdown`. Once those packages are installed, the article
requires no network, hospital connection, external dataset, or prepared model.

# Simulate Harbor General's extracts

We create a larger **historical** cohort for model training and eight separate
**current** encounters for the operational walkthrough. The tables resemble
patient demographics, encounter/discharge records, post-discharge observations,
and terminal-event feeds. The observation is recorded four days after discharge
and becomes available a day later. Event records also have distinct occurrence
and availability times.

```{r simulate}
set.seed(6404)
day <- 24 * 60 * 60
origin <- as.POSIXct("2026-01-01 00:00:00", tz = "UTC")
n_history <- 420L

historical_patients <- tibble(
  patient_id = sprintf("H%03d", seq_len(n_history)),
  age = sample(45:88, n_history, replace = TRUE)
)
historical_encounters <- tibble(
  encounter_id = sprintf("EH%03d", seq_len(n_history)),
  patient_id = historical_patients$patient_id,
  admission_time = origin - (80 - sample(0:20, n_history, replace = TRUE)) * day,
  acuity = sample(0:2, n_history, replace = TRUE),
  cohort = "historical"
) |>
  mutate(discharge_time = admission_time + sample(2:5, n_history, replace = TRUE) * day)
historical_observations <- historical_encounters |>
  transmute(
    encounter_id,
    signal = rbinom(n(), 1, plogis(-0.3 + 0.4 * acuity)),
    observed_at = discharge_time + 4 * day,
    available_at = discharge_time + 5 * day
  )

# Simulate later readmission and death outcomes for the historical cohort.
readmit_probability <- plogis(
  -2 + 0.025 * (historical_patients$age - 65) +
    0.35 * historical_encounters$acuity + 0.45 * historical_observations$signal
)
readmit_day <- ifelse(
  runif(n_history) < readmit_probability,
  sample(4:27, n_history, replace = TRUE), NA_integer_
)
death_day <- ifelse(
  runif(n_history) < 0.06,
  sample(4:27, n_history, replace = TRUE), NA_integer_
)
# A death before a simulated readmission prevents that later readmission.
readmit_day[!is.na(death_day) & !is.na(readmit_day) &
              death_day < readmit_day] <- NA_integer_
historical_readmissions <- historical_encounters |>
  mutate(event_day = readmit_day) |>
  filter(!is.na(event_day)) |>
  transmute(
    event_id = paste0("HR-", encounter_id), encounter_id,
    event_type = "readmission",
    occurred_at = discharge_time + event_day * day,
    available_at = occurred_at + sample(0:2, n(), replace = TRUE) * day
  )
historical_deaths <- historical_encounters |>
  mutate(event_day = death_day) |>
  filter(!is.na(event_day)) |>
  transmute(
    event_id = paste0("HD-", encounter_id), encounter_id,
    event_type = "death",
    occurred_at = discharge_time + event_day * day,
    available_at = occurred_at + sample(0:2, n(), replace = TRUE) * day
  )

current_patients <- tibble(
  patient_id = paste0("C", 1:8),
  age = c(72, 64, 61, NA, 70, 58, 68, 77)
)
current_encounters <- tibble(
  encounter_id = paste0("E", 1:8),
  patient_id = current_patients$patient_id,
  discharge_time = origin + c(0, 2, 6, 1, -27, 8, 14, 0) * day,
  acuity = c(2, 1, 0, 2, 1, 1, 2, 0),
  cohort = "current"
) |>
  mutate(admission_time = discharge_time - 2 * day)
current_observations <- current_encounters |>
  transmute(
    encounter_id, signal = c(1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0),
    observed_at = discharge_time + 4 * day,
    available_at = discharge_time + 5 * day
  )
current_events <- tibble(
  event_id = c("ER-E1", "ED-E2"),
  encounter_id = c("E1", "E2"),
  event_type = c("readmission", "death"),
  occurred_at = origin + c(8.5, 13) * day,
  available_at = origin + c(10.5, 13.5) * day
)

patients <- bind_rows(historical_patients, current_patients)
encounters <- bind_rows(historical_encounters, current_encounters)
observations <- bind_rows(historical_observations, current_observations)
events <- bind_rows(historical_readmissions, historical_deaths, current_events)
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(patients$patient_id),
  !anyDuplicated(encounters$encounter_id),
  !anyDuplicated(events$event_id),
  all(encounters$patient_id %in% patients$patient_id),
  all(events$encounter_id %in% encounters$encounter_id),
  all(events$occurred_at <= events$available_at)
)
current_encounters |>
  select(encounter_id, patient_id, discharge_time, acuity)
current_events |>
  select(encounter_id, event_type, occurred_at, available_at)
```

The first current readmission occurs on January 9 but is not available until
January 11. The second current terminal event is a death. Encounter E4 has no
age; its otherwise eligible episode will illustrate a provider failure. E5's
follow-up window has already closed by the first assessment. E3, E6, and E7
enter the supplied discharge population on different days.

# Create a project and map the sources

`rrp_project_init()` creates an ordinary, editable project. The two R scripts
start as deliberate stubs: initialization does **not** supply a working hospital
model or source connection. We save our simulated extracts inside this project
only because Harbor General is fictional; a real organization would connect
its own sources and keep their access details under its control.

```{r project}
work_dir <- tempfile("harbor-general-")
dir.create(work_dir)
project <- rrp_project_init(file.path(work_dir, "harbor-rrp"), "harbor-general")
dir.create(file.path(project, "source"))
saveRDS(patients, file.path(project, "source", "patients.rds"))
saveRDS(encounters, file.path(project, "source", "encounters.rds"))
saveRDS(observations, file.path(project, "source", "observations.rds"))
saveRDS(events, file.path(project, "source", "events.rds"))
list.files(project)
```

The project contains configuration and branding, `R/produce-canonical.R` for
source mapping, `R/calculate-risk.R` for the hospital's provider, and `app/` for
the project-owned Shiny interface. `state/` and generated products appear only
when we initialize history and refresh products later. The mapper below reads
the extracts, joins encounters to patient identities, and returns the two
required canonical data frames. It supplies all current encounters discharged
by `as_of_time`; omitting earlier eligible patients from a later operational
snapshot would change the current pool. The package derives the 30-day endpoint
and applies eligibility rules.

```{r mapper}
mapper_code <- r"---(
rrp_produce_canonical <- function(project_root, as_of_time) {
  source_dir <- file.path(project_root, "source")
  patients <- readRDS(file.path(source_dir, "patients.rds"))
  encounters <- readRDS(file.path(source_dir, "encounters.rds"))
  events <- readRDS(file.path(source_dir, "events.rds"))

  selected <- encounters |>
    dplyr::filter(cohort == "current", discharge_time <= as_of_time) |>
    dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(patients, patient_id), by = "patient_id")
  discharge_episode <- selected |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      episode_id = paste0("episode-", encounter_id),
      patient_id,
      index_encounter_id = encounter_id,
      admission_time, discharge_time
    )
  terminal_event <- events |>
    dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(selected, encounter_id), by = "encounter_id") |>
    dplyr::filter(occurred_at <= as_of_time, available_at <= as_of_time) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      terminal_event_id = event_id,
      episode_id = paste0("episode-", encounter_id),
      event_type, occurred_at, available_at
    )
  list(
    discharge_episode = as.data.frame(discharge_episode),
    terminal_event = as.data.frame(terminal_event)
  )
}
)---"
writeLines(mapper_code, file.path(project, "R", "produce-canonical.R"))
```

The occurrence and availability filters ensure the January 9 readmission is
absent from the January 10 source snapshot and present on January 12 with its
original occurrence time. These are distinct facts, not a later rewrite of the
January 10 result. The canonical tables contain only shared episode and event
facts; the age, acuity, and post-discharge observation stay private to the
hospital's provider.

# Fit a remaining-risk demonstration model

We construct **landmark** training rows at days 2, 7, and 14 after each
historical discharge. A row is included while no readmission or death is
*known* by that time. Its outcome is a first readmission strictly after the
landmark and before a competing death, through that discharge's day-30 endpoint.
The outcome is learned retrospectively, but predictors use only information
available at the landmark. This is a small educational logistic model of the
remaining interval, not an unchanged discharge-time classifier. Its repeated
rows per encounter and simplified source process are not a clinical validation
or a claim of calibrated risk.

```{r train}
historical_event_times <- events |>
  semi_join(historical_encounters, by = "encounter_id") |>
  select(encounter_id, event_type, occurred_at, available_at) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = event_type,
    values_from = c(occurred_at, available_at),
    names_glue = "{.value}_{event_type}"
  )

training <- tidyr::crossing(
  encounter_id = historical_encounters$encounter_id,
  landmark_day = c(2L, 7L, 14L)
) |>
  left_join(historical_encounters, by = "encounter_id") |>
  left_join(historical_patients, by = "patient_id") |>
  left_join(historical_observations |>
              select(encounter_id, signal, signal_available_at = available_at),
            by = "encounter_id") |>
  left_join(historical_event_times, by = "encounter_id") |>
  mutate(
    as_of_time = discharge_time + landmark_day * day,
    followup_end = discharge_time + 30 * day,
    age_scaled = (age - 65) / 10,
    days_remaining = 30 - landmark_day,
    signal_as_of = if_else(signal_available_at <= as_of_time, signal, 0L)
  ) |>
  filter(
    is.na(occurred_at_readmission) |
      occurred_at_readmission > as_of_time |
      available_at_readmission > as_of_time,
    is.na(occurred_at_death) |
      occurred_at_death > as_of_time |
      available_at_death > as_of_time
  ) |>
  mutate(
    outcome = as.integer(
      !is.na(occurred_at_readmission) &
        occurred_at_readmission > as_of_time &
        occurred_at_readmission <= followup_end &
        (is.na(occurred_at_death) |
           occurred_at_readmission <= occurred_at_death)
    )
  )
training |>
  count(landmark_day, outcome)

model <- stats::glm(
  outcome ~ age_scaled + acuity + signal_as_of + days_remaining,
  family = stats::binomial(), data = training
)
round(stats::coef(model), 3)
dir.create(file.path(project, "model"))
model_path <- file.path(project, "model", "landmark-glm.rds")
saveRDS(model, model_path)
stopifnot(inherits(readRDS(model_path), "glm"))
```

The model uses remaining days and a post-discharge signal only once that signal
is available. Death before a future readmission makes the training outcome
zero. Harbor General's current encounters were **not** model-training cases;
we do not use their outcomes to fit the model or present its predictions as a
performance evaluation.

# Supply the hospital's risk provider

`readmit` asks the project provider for one eligible episode at a time. The
request gives the episode identity, assessment time, and fixed follow-up
endpoint. The provider reads private source information and the saved model
from its own project directory. E4 has no age, so it reports a failure rather
than inventing a probability. An organization must assess its own predictor
quality and timing; `readmit` does not validate them.

```{r provider}
provider_code <- r"---(
rrp_calculate_risk <- function(project_root, request) {
  source_dir <- file.path(project_root, "source")
  patients <- readRDS(file.path(source_dir, "patients.rds"))
  encounters <- readRDS(file.path(source_dir, "encounters.rds"))
  observations <- readRDS(file.path(source_dir, "observations.rds"))

  patient <- patients[patients$patient_id == request$patient_id, , drop = FALSE]
  encounter <- encounters[
    encounters$encounter_id == request$index_encounter_id, , drop = FALSE
  ]
  if (nrow(patient) != 1L || is.na(patient$age[[1L]])) {
    return(list(failure = "Patient age unavailable"))
  }
  if (nrow(encounter) != 1L) {
    return(list(failure = "Encounter unavailable"))
  }
  available <- observations[
    observations$encounter_id == request$index_encounter_id &
      observations$available_at <= request$as_of_time, , drop = FALSE
  ]
  signal_as_of <- if (nrow(available)) {
    available$signal[[which.max(available$available_at)]]
  } else {
    0L
  }
  newdata <- data.frame(
    age_scaled = (patient$age[[1L]] - 65) / 10,
    acuity = encounter$acuity[[1L]],
    signal_as_of = signal_as_of,
    days_remaining = request$remaining_seconds / (24 * 60 * 60)
  )
  model <- readRDS(file.path(project_root, "model", "landmark-glm.rds"))
  probability <- as.numeric(stats::predict(model, newdata, type = "response"))
  list(probability = probability)
}
)---"
writeLines(provider_code, file.path(project, "R", "calculate-risk.R"))
rrp_project_validate(project)
```

Validation confirms that the project files and function signatures load. It
does not call either function or certify the simulated clinical definitions,
model, or predictions. The following real runs exercise those interfaces.

# Assess repeatedly and inspect history

At January 6, E3, E6, and E7 have not yet been discharged. At January 10, E1's
readmission has occurred but is not yet available; E1 remains eligible based on
what the process knows. By January 12 it is a known readmission. E2 later
becomes ineligible after its known death. E4 remains eligible but has an
unavailable model estimate. The model's remaining-time and newly available
observation inputs can change estimates for other episodes.

```{r runs}
rrp_state_init(project)
assessment_times <- origin + c(5.5, 9.5, 11.5, 15.5) * day
runs <- lapply(assessment_times, function(time) rrp_run(project, time))
run_summary <- tibble(
  as_of_time = assessment_times,
  accepted = vapply(runs, `[[`, integer(1), "accepted"),
  provider_failures = vapply(runs, `[[`, integer(1), "provider_failures"),
  ineligible = vapply(runs, `[[`, integer(1), "ineligible")
)
run_summary

# A later-executed historical backfill does not replace the newest snapshot.
backfill <- rrp_run(project, assessment_times[[2L]])
status <- rrp_project_status(project)
status[c("state_initialized", "run_count")]
history <- rrp_inspect_history(project)
history |>
  filter(patient_id %in% c("C1", "C2", "C3", "C4")) |>
  select(patient_id, as_of_time, disposition, probability,
         terminal_occurred_at, terminal_available_at) |>
  arrange(patient_id, as_of_time) |>
  head(22)
```

The retained January 10 E1 row remains an accepted assessment after the
January 12 run records a known readmission. E4's provider failure is an episode
outcome, not zero risk. The backfill creates another run at the January 10
analytical time; history keeps both. Status reports the most recently *recorded*
run, which is now the backfill.

We can independently compare E3's latest accepted probability with a direct
prediction from the saved model. E3's observation is available by January 16.

```{r model-check}
e3_time <- assessment_times[[4L]]
e3 <- current_encounters |> filter(encounter_id == "E3")
e3_age <- current_patients$age[current_patients$patient_id == "C3"]
e3_expected <- as.numeric(stats::predict(
  readRDS(model_path),
  newdata = data.frame(
    age_scaled = (e3_age - 65) / 10,
    acuity = e3$acuity,
    signal_as_of = current_observations$signal[
      current_observations$encounter_id == "E3"
    ],
    days_remaining = as.numeric(difftime(
      e3$discharge_time + 30 * day, e3_time, units = "days"
    ))
  ),
  type = "response"
))
e3_recorded <- history |>
  filter(episode_id == "episode-E3", as_of_time == e3_time) |>
  pull(probability)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(e3_recorded, e3_expected)))
tibble(recorded = e3_recorded, direct_model_prediction = e3_expected)
```

# Generate and interpret the products

`rrp_refresh_products()` reads retained history; it does not call the mapper or
provider again. The current snapshot is the completed run with the greatest
analytical time, even though we executed an older backfill last. Supplying a
partial population at a later analytical time would make that partial run the
current snapshot; the platform does not merge missing episodes from older runs.
An operational mapper should supply the complete relevant discharge cohort.

```{r products}
products <- rrp_refresh_products(project)
stopifnot(products$selected_run_id == runs[[4L]]$run_id,
          status$latest_run_id == backfill$run_id)
current_risk <- read.csv(products$files[["current_risk"]])
trajectory <- read.csv(products$files[["trajectory"]])
scope <- read.csv(products$files[["scope"]])
current_risk |>
  select(episode_id, disposition, probability)
trajectory |>
  filter(episode_id == "episode-E3") |>
  select(episode_id, as_of_time, probability)
scope |>
  select(episodes_assessed, eligible_count, accepted_count,
         provider_failure_count, known_readmission_count,
         known_death_count, window_closed_count)
```

**Current remaining risk** includes the latest eligible episodes; E4 remains
there with a missing probability. **Remaining-risk trajectory** lists actual
accepted assessments for episodes still in the current pool, including both
January 10 runs; its observations are not a continuous risk curve. **Operational
scope** counts accepted, failed, and ineligible outcomes in the selected
January 16 run. E1 and E2 are absent from the current pool because their
terminal events are known; E5's window is closed. The CSVs are derived outputs,
while history retains each completed assessment.

# Explore and customize the project app

The project app already existed before our first assessment and would have
opened with empty views. After refresh it reads the three product CSVs. Its
**Current Risk Pool** shows accepted and provider-failed eligible episodes;
selecting a row reveals its current estimate and recorded accepted trajectory.
**Overview** shows operational counts and summaries of available current
estimates. The app's Reload Data control rereads CSVs, but does not run an
assessment or refresh products.

Install `shiny`, `bslib`, `reactable`, `plotly`, and `yaml` in the environment
that will run the app. Launch it manually with the following command; the
article does not launch an interactive session while rendering.

```r
shiny::runApp(file.path(project, "app"))
```

Harbor General can replace its project logo without changing the package. We
generate a simple PNG in the exact path named by the project's `_brand.yml`.
Then we append one small color rule to the project-owned stylesheet; the shared
package template is untouched. These are examples of ownership, not a new
customization framework.

```{r customize}
logo_path <- file.path(project, "assets", "project-logo.png")
grDevices::png(logo_path, width = 520, height = 150, bg = "white")
graphics::plot.new()
graphics::rect(0, 0, 1, 1, col = "#174D58", border = NA)
graphics::text(0.5, 0.53, "HARBOR GENERAL", col = "white",
               cex = 1.8, font = 2)
grDevices::dev.off()

css_path <- file.path(project, "app", "www", "rrp.css")
cat("\n/* Harbor General project styling */\n",
    ".rrp-page-intro h1 { color: #174D58; }\n",
    file = css_path, append = TRUE)
stopifnot(file.exists(logo_path), file.info(logo_path)$size > 0,
          grepl("assets/project-logo.png", readLines(file.path(project, "_brand.yml")),
                fixed = TRUE) |> any(),
          grepl("Harbor General project styling", readLines(css_path),
                fixed = TRUE) |> any())
```

For a hosted app, Posit Connect or Posit Connect Cloud are possible deployment
choices. The deployment would need the app's runtime packages, this project's
app, assets, model, and generated products. The hospital also needs a deliberate
way to retain project history and run assessments separately from app hosting;
the app only reads products. This walkthrough does not deploy or validate a
production service.
